name: Onboarding Dashboard
user_goal: New merchant is guided to create their first offer with minimal friction; returning merchant gets a working hub to monitor offers, theme-extension status, and setup progress.

entry_points.path: Shopify Admin -> App -> Home (first load after install)
entry_points.precondition: Store has 0 existing offers of any status (first-time store, never created an offer)
Store has created >=1 offer at some point in its history, even if later deleted or reinstalled

entry_points.path: Home -> 'Create offer' CTA (onboarding empty-state card) Setup Guide Step 1 'Create offer' button
entry_points.precondition: Onboarding empty-state is showing, or Setup Guide Step 1 not yet completed

entry_points.path: Home -> Theme Extension Status block 'Enable theme app' button, or Setup Guide Step 2 'Enable theme app extension' button

capabilities.name: Auto-detect first-time vs. returning merchant (onboarding <-> dashboard switch)
capabilities.description: Decides whether Home shows the onboarding empty-state or the full dashboard, based on whether the store has ever created an offer (any offer type, any status). The switch is one-directional and sticky: once a store has had >=1 offer, it never reverts to onboarding again, even after deleting all offers or reinstalling the app -- and the switch itself is lazy, only evaluated on the next Home navigation, not pushed live across other open sessions.

capabilities.name: First-run onboarding empty-state (guided first offer creation, B4S compliance)
capabilities.description: Immediately post-install, Home renders a dedicated onboarding view (header, primary CTA, empty-state card) that guides the merchant to create their first offer. This view's presence is a direct fix for a Shopify App Store review flag (B4S), so a regression here carries App Store risk, not just a UX bug.

capabilities.name: Dashboard hub: recent offers list & storefront click stat
capabilities.description: Once unlocked, the dashboard view's 3-section layout includes a 'Recently created offers' list (5 most recent, any status, with 'Manage offers'/'Create offer' navigation buttons -- this supersedes an older paginated-table spec) and a 30-day add-to-cart click stat widget.

capabilities.name: Theme Extension Status indicator + one-click enable (deep-link)
capabilities.description: A permanent status block shows whether the theme app extension is Active or Inactive, with contextual helper text and a 'Need help?' support-chat button. When Inactive, an 'Enable theme app' button deep-links into the Shopify Theme Editor (auto-selects the active/published theme, auto-inserts the app block, prompts Save). The block also reflects toggles made externally in the theme editor, and still shows the correct state even if the merchant closes the editor tab without saving. This block fully replaced an older transient warning banner (QVD-31, retired by QVD-66) -- the banner reappearing alongside the block is a regression, not a feature.

capabilities.name: Setup Guide checklist (2-step onboarding progress tracker)
capabilities.description: A 2-step checklist (Step 1: create an offer; Step 2: enable theme app extension, reusing the same deep-link mechanism as the Theme Extension Status block) with a dynamically updating progress tracker ('1/2 completed' etc.). Once both steps are done it shows '2/2 completed' and auto-collapses, but the merchant can still click to re-expand and review the steps afterward.

state_transitions.condition: Offer count transitions 0 -> >=1, counted across any offer status (paused/expired included, no 'draft' status exists); the switch does NOT happen immediately on offer creation -- the merchant stays on the offer-settings page, and the view only changes the next time they navigate back to Home themselves

state_transitions.trigger: Merchant deletes the only/all remaining offers
state_transitions.condition: Store has previously had >=1 offer at any point -- dashboard persists and onboarding does NOT reappear

state_transitions.to: onboarding_empty_state (if never created an offer) OR dashboard_view (if ever created one, even if later deleted)
state_transitions.condition: Depends entirely on the store instance's historical offer-creation, not its current offer count

state_transitions.trigger: Merchant clicks 'Enable theme app' (status block or Setup Guide Step 2), completes the Theme Editor flow and clicks Save -- OR toggles the extension directly from the Shopify theme editor outside the app
state_transitions.condition: Status block reflects the change either way, with no in-app action required for the external-toggle path

state_transitions.trigger: Both Step 1 (create offer) and Step 2 (enable theme app extension) are completed
Merchant clicks to expand the collapsed Setup Guide

confirmed_rules.statement: Onboarding auto-shows only for first-time stores with 0 existing offers; once >=1 offer exists, onboarding stops auto-showing and the dashboard view takes over (QVD-18 AC).
'Existing offers' for the 0-vs->=1 threshold counts every offer status (e.g. paused/expired), not active-only -- consistent with the Recently-created-offers list also showing any status.
Offers in this app have no 'draft' status.

Onboarding must render on Home immediately post-install with a step-by-step setup guide and clear primary CTAs -- a direct fix for a Shopify review (B4S) flag, so regressions here carry App Store risk.

Onboarding view content: header 'Hello {{Store name}}!', primary CTA 'Create offer', empty-state card with 'Create your first deal!' 'Create your first volume discount offer to get started.' 'Create offer' button.
Dashboard view has 3 sections: Theme Extension Status, Setup Guide, 'Recently created offers'.
'Recently created offers' lists the 5 most recently created offers regardless of status -- supersedes the original QVD-27 paginated-table spec (Name/Status/Trigger/Combination/Actions columns).
'Recently created offers' section has 'Manage offers' and 'Create offer' navigation buttons.
Theme Extension Status Active state shows status 'Active', helper text 'The created offer is visible on your storefront.', and a 'Need help?' button opening in-app chat with customer support.
Theme Extension Status Inactive state shows status 'Inactive', explanatory helper text, the same 'Need help?' button, plus an 'Enable theme app' button that opens the Shopify Theme Editor.

The QVD-31 transient warning banner is retired (QVD-66): current behavior is banner absent, status block present. A banner reappearing alongside the status block is a regression to QVD-31 behavior, not a new feature.

Clicking 'Enable theme app' redirects to the Shopify Theme Editor in a new tab, auto-selects 'the correct theme', auto-inserts the 'Qikify: Volume Discount' app block into the relevant section (typically product page), and instructs the merchant to click Save to apply. This deep-link mechanism (from QVD-31) was NOT superseded by QVD-66 -- only the standalone warning banner was.
'The correct theme' auto-selected by the deep-link = the theme currently active/published on the storefront.
Setup Guide has a dynamically updating progress tracker (e.g. '1/2 completed'); at '2/2 completed' the guide auto-collapses.
Setup Guide Step 1: description about creating an offer matching sales strategy; 'Create offer' (Primary) button opens the offer settings page.
Setup Guide Step 2: description about enabling theme app extension to make the offer visible on storefront; 'Enable theme app extension' (Primary) button opens the theme editor.
Setup Guide Step 2's button reuses the exact same deep-link mechanism as the Theme Extension Status block's button.
Dashboard ATC (add-to-cart) click stat (QVD-115) shows a 30-day click count.

Creating the first offer does not auto-redirect to Home/Dashboard -- merchant stays on the offer settings page; the switch to Dashboard only happens the next time they navigate back to Home themselves.
Deleting the only/all offers does not revert the dashboard to onboarding, once the store has ever had >=1 offer.

Reinstall behavior depends on the store's historical offer-creation, not current offer count: never created -> onboarding reappears; previously created (even if later deleted) -> dashboard shows, onboarding stays hidden.
Toggling the theme app extension externally from the Shopify theme editor is reflected in the Theme Extension Status block without any in-app action.
Rapid repeated clicks on the 'Create offer' CTA carry no double-click risk, because the first click already navigates away to the offer-type selection page before a second click can register.

With multiple staff accounts viewing Home simultaneously, state is store-wide but not push/live-updated: a staff member who already has Home open keeps seeing Onboarding until they reload, even if another staff member just created an offer.
Closing/navigating away from the Theme Editor tab without clicking Save still leaves the Theme Extension Status block correctly showing 'Inactive'.
After the Setup Guide auto-collapses (2/2 done), the merchant can click to expand it again to view the steps.

portal.element: Onboarding empty-state view (header, primary CTA, empty-state card)
'Recently created offers' list + 'Manage offers'/'Create offer' nav buttons
Theme Extension Status block (Active/Inactive states, 'Need help?' button, 'Enable theme app' button)
Setup Guide (progress tracker, Step 1, Step 2, collapse/expand)

dependencies.feature: discount-offers object (quantity-break multibuy-mix-match-combo wholesale-pricing-offer -- any offer type)
dependencies.relationship: The onboarding<->dashboard switch and its stickiness are driven purely by whether the store has ever created an offer of ANY type/status, not by this feature's own data -- this feature's core trigger logic depends on offer existence owned by the discount-offers object.

dependencies.feature: analytics ("Analytics", out of this shard's scope)
dependencies.relationship: UNRESOLVED -- source doc does not state whether the Dashboard ATC click stat (KB-018) and the standalone Analytics feature's metric are the same underlying counter or two independent ones. See unknown_areas.

risks.risk: Onboarding empty-state is a direct fix for a Shopify App Store review flag (B4S); a regression in its post-install render carries App Store compliance risk, not just a UX bug.

The retired QVD-31 warning banner reappearing alongside the current Theme Extension Status block is a regression back to pre-QVD-66 behavior and must be flagged as a defect, not assumed to be an intentional new feature.
Multi-staff/simultaneous-session Home view is not live-updated; a QA tester running 2 sessions could misread the stale onboarding/dashboard state as a bug when it is documented, expected behavior.

unknown_areas.question: What is the exact truncation/overflow behavior of the onboarding header 'Hello {{Store name}}!' for unusually long store names, special characters, or emoji?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Directly affects onboarding header rendering; the source doc flags this as an untested edge case with no resolved expected behavior -- QA cannot assert a specific oracle here without guessing.

unknown_areas.question: Is the Dashboard ATC click stat (KB-018, QVD-115) the same underlying metric/counter as the standalone Analytics feature's ("Analytics") metric, or an independent counter?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: The source doc only says it is 'a metric hosted on the dashboard, not core onboarding/dashboard logic' and points to the Analytics doc without confirming identity. Treating them as the same when they are not (or vice versa) risks double-counting or silently dropping coverage of one of the two in test planning.

unknown_areas.question: What staff permission level, if any, is required to view Home, click 'Create offer', or click 'Enable theme app extension'?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: No permission/role model is stated anywhere in the source doc for this feature. Without it, access-control regressions (e.g. a lower-permission staff account unexpectedly gaining or losing access to these actions) have no documented oracle to test against.

unknown_areas.question: Is the onboarding<->dashboard state and setup-guide progress derived purely client-side from the offer list at render time, or is there a dedicated backend endpoint/table/cache behind it that could itself go stale or fail independently?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: No API, DB, or code-level evidence exists anywhere in the source doc set for this feature (confirmed against the scope-plan's own coverage grid: db/code both flagged MISSING/P3, api not even listed). Backend-side regressions in this area currently have zero oracle coverage.
